searchText: Something for the agenda if it isn't already - regarding what to do if block not found. There’s hive tests for eth_getBlockReceipts but fixing these hive tests broke hive tests for eth_simulate that use a future block, since besu has have common error handling for RPCs. Is it expected that we would want different behavior here or should eth_simulate also return null if the requested block is not found? more context here on this draft besu PR https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/9303 (also this indicates there’s a gap in rpc-compat hive tests for error handling for other RPCs eg eth_getBalance, eth_getCode that will have the same issue/question) It looks like geth nethermind reth are all returning an error here, just with different error codes. I can see both points: stick to the usual approach of returning nil, but also see the point of returning an explicit error because of the complexity of eth_simulate and the many things that can go wrong. Note here about nethermind. we are going with the more strict parsing for block params and hashes. There is a flag you can change to go back to the loose parsing we had previously. implementation here: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/9489 Something for the agenda if it isn't

Something for the agenda if it isn't already - regarding what to do if block not found.

There’s hive tests for eth_getBlockReceipts
but fixing these hive tests broke hive tests for eth_simulate that use a future block, since besu has have common error handling for RPCs. 

Is it expected that we would want different behavior here or should eth_simulate also return null if the requested block is not found?
more context here on this draft besu PR https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/9303

(also this indicates there’s a gap in rpc-compat hive tests for error handling for other RPCs eg eth_getBalance, eth_getCode that will have the same issue/question)
